recipient: Democratic Republic of the Congo
title: African Development Bank — DRC second general population and housing census (RGPH-2), 2026
description: "The African Development Bank Group has announced an $80 million contribution towards the Democratic Republic of the Congo's second General Population and Housing Census (RGPH2)." "The announcement was made on 23 March 2026 in Kinshasa during a donor roundtable convening the census's technical and financial partners. The Bank's $80 million contribution represents a significant share of the $200 million in total commitments announced at the event." "Of the Bank Group's commitment, $50 million will fund census operations, while $30 million will support capacity-building for national institutions including the National Institute of Statistics (INS) and those involved in the planning, programming, budgeting, and monitoring and evaluation (PPBME) chain."

recipient: Eastcastle Infrastructure DRC SARLU
title: Eastcastle Debt II — shared telecom tower infrastructure, DR Congo
description:
Eastcastle Infrastructure DRC SARLU (Eastcastle DRC or the Company) is a subsidiary of Eastcastle Infrastructure Limited (Eastcastle Infrastructure), which was established in 2020 as a platform company to own and operate shared telecom tower infrastructure in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Nigeria. Eastcastle Infrastructure and Eastcastle DRC are existing IFC clients, with environmental and social (E&S) performance assessed as satisfactory. An Environmental and Social Review Summary (ESRS) for IFC's initial equity investment in Eastcastle Infrastructure was publicly disclosed in 2021 (https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/44090/eastcastle). IFC subsequently disclosed an ESRS in connection with a further US$30 million debt facility provided to Eastcastle DRC in 2023 (https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/46563/eastcastle-debt).

The development impact thesis derives from the Company's potential to enhance mobile broadband capacity for MNOs in the DRC to help improve quality of connectivity for end users and mitigate environmental impact through infrastructure sharing and energy mix strategy. Beyond the Company, this initiative is anticipated to strengthen competitiveness in the tower sharing market.

title: Helios Towers — DRC telecom tower infrastructure investment, 2026
description: "L'Agence nationale pour la promotion des investissements (Anapi) et Helios Towers DRC... ont procédé ce mardi à la signature d'une convention d'investissement estimée à plus de 100 millions USD." The investment aims "à étendre la connectivité aussi bien à Kinshasa que dans les provinces." "Plus de 4 000 emplois ont déjà été créés." The agreement supports the Plan national du numérique et de l'inclusion 2025 and the "DRC Digital 2030" project.

recipient: DRC Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Affairs
title: Genew Technologies — DRC Congo River fibre-optic MoU, 2026
description: "The Democratic Republic of the Congo has partnered with China's Genew Technologies to build a fiber-optic route along the Congo River worth US$1.5 billion. The two entities signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) for the fiber deployment project. The project covers about 2,100km of infrastructure, including 1,700km of fiber-optic cable along the Congo River from Muanda to Kisangani and nearly 400km of terrestrial connections." Genew CEO Wu Minhua said the total cost is estimated at $1.5 billion, with more than $400 million required for the first phase.

recipient: Raxio DRC
title: Raxio Group — Raxio DRC1 data centre, Kinshasa, 2023
description: "Known as Raxio DRC1, the cutting-edge facility is backed by a $30 million investment, and represents a pivotal milestone in the nation's Plan National du Numérique." "Located in Limete on the southeast of Kinshasa, the two-storey Raxio Data Centre spans 1,542 square meters. Its modern design can house up to 400 racks and can reliably deliver 1.5MW of IT power to customer equipment." "The project was completed in record time since breaking ground on construction in early 2023."

recipient: Eastcastle Infrastructure
title: Eastcastle DRC Telecom Tower Platform - EAIF
description: EAIF provided a USD 30 million commitment to Eastcastle Infrastructure, a TowerCo platform owning, operating and developing shared telecom tower infrastructure in DRC. The investment enables purchase and development of telecom towers across DRC for mobile network operators (MNOs), supporting digital transformation and last-mile connectivity. DRC's mobile subscriber market projected to grow by 22 million subscribers by 2030.

recipient: Airtel Mobile Commerce
title: Airtel Mobile Money Congo, Democratic Republic of – Digital Financial Services Guarantee
description: MIGA political risk guarantee covering The Rise Fund II Aurora S.à r.l. (TPG private equity) equity investment in Airtel Mobile Commerce B.V.'s subsidiary providing Airtel Money digital financial services in Congo, Democratic Republic of. Services include mobile wallet (cash-in/cash-out), airtime recharging, bill payments, merchant payments; with international transfers, savings and microloans in some markets. Risks: war and civil disturbance, expropriation, transfer restriction and inconvertibility for up to 5 years.

recipient: Democratic Republic of Congo
title: BANDWIDTH AND CLOUD SOLUTIONS (BCS) DRC FIBRE PHASE 2
description: Second phase of construction of a fibre optic backbone in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), focusing on underserved areas of eastern DRC. The fibre links will enable high-speed broadband in nine towns, deployed along railways (1,280 km) and roads (139 km). ~1,400 km of new fibre optics in underserved regions of eastern DRC. First quasi-equity financing from EIB Global.

recipient: Bandwidth and Cloud Services Group Holdings (BCS)
title: Bandwidth and Cloud Services Group (BCS) DRC Expansion
description: Finnfund provided a USD 12 million senior loan to BCS Group to finance its DRC expansion, building fibre-optic backbone and broadband network infrastructure in East, Central and Southern Africa. BCS provides wholesale broadband and internet services to ISPs, telecoms, corporates and governments, improving internet reliability, accessibility and affordability.

recipient: Democratic Republic of the Congo Ministry of Economy and Finance
title: China Eximbank provides RMB 1.05 billion government concessional loan for Ministry of Finance Information and Communications Technology Modernization Project
description: In the first quarter of 2020, China Eximbank and the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo signed an RMB 1,050,000,000 government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Ministry of Finance ICT Modernization Project. The borrowing terms of the GCL are as follows: a 20-year maturity, a 5-year grace period, a 2% interest rate, and a 0.25% commitment fee. However, it is known that the borrower was expected to use the GCL proceeds to finance a commercial contract with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. worth approximately $150 million that was signed in 2014.    The purpose of the project is to modernize the computer systems of three state financial authorities: the General Directorate of Taxes (DGI), the General Directorate of Customs and Excise (DGDA) and the General Directorate of Administrative, Judicial, State and Shareholding Revenue (DGRAD).   Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. is the contractor responsible for implementation. As of August 2020, the China Eximbank loan for the project had not yet been disbursed. A Tier 3 data centre at the DRC Ministry of Finance was inaugurated in November 2023 (wearetech.africa, via the BU GDP China Loans to Africa database).

recipient: Helios Towers DRC Infraco SPRL
